original_value: We present UbiquiTouch, an ultra low power wireless touch interface. With an average power consumption of 30.91μW, UbiquiTouch can run on energy harvested from ambient light. It achieves this performance through low power touch sensing and passive communication to a nearby smartphone using ambient FM backscatter. This approach allows UbiquiTouch to be deployed in mobile situations both in indoor and outdoor locations, without the need for any additional infrastructure for operation. To demonstrate the potential of this technology, we evaluate it in several different and realistic scenarios. Finally, we address the future application space for this technology.

result.paraphrase: UbiquiTouch is introduced as an ultra-low-power wireless touch interface. With average power use of 30.91 μW, it can operate on energy harvested from ambient light. Its performance comes from low-power touch sensing and passive communication to a nearby smartphone via ambient FM backscatter. This enables deployment in mobile settings indoors and outdoors, without requiring any extra infrastructure to function. To show the technology’s potential, it is evaluated across several realistic scenarios, and the future application space for it is then discussed.
